refractiveIndex.source: SCAQMD Method 317-93 (approved May 1993, revised August 1996), Table 1 'Optical properties of natural fibers' (compiled from The Particle Atlas): 'Animal' (hair), length 1.55, cross 1.54; wool, length 1.556, cross 1.547; https://www.aqmd.gov/docs/default-source/laboratory-procedures/methods-procedures/317-93.pdf
refractiveIndex.derivation: (n_par + 2 n_perp)/3: animal hair (1.55 + 2 x 1.54)/3 = 1.543; wool (1.556 + 2 x 1.547)/3 = 1.550. Mohair is a keratin hair, so 1.55.
refractiveIndex.note: Checked against the PDF. The table's row is headed 'Animal', generic animal hair; there is no mohair row, so mohair is taken as a keratin hair between the two rows. The present 1.46 (grade 'record') is Sadeghi et al.'s fitted model eta from velvet.json. As the silk record says of its own eta, that is a fitted model parameter, not a fibre index. It is a poor value for dielectric.refractiveIndex and should stay only in optics.clothModelVelvet. The cotton ground (about 1.53-1.58) is hidden by the pile. This is outside the 'unverified' remit.

porosity.note: A pile is mostly air; no measured porosity was read.

wettingDepth.source: Substances/velvet.json: unverified pile height (1 to 3 mm)

grain.note: The finest structure the cloth shows: its thread or fibre tufts.

bed.note: The length of the yarn's slubs, the coarsest unevenness the cloth shows.

bedAspect.note: Slubs run along the thread: how much longer than wide.

hurst.note: A first self-affinity for a yarn's unevenness.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of the dye's tone across the cloth.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range across the cloth.

roughness.derivation: sqrt(tan 6 deg): the Slab roughness whose GGX width is the fitted surface spread

sheen.note: A velvet is all pile: its sheen is at full weight.

sheenRoughness.note: A cut pile sends its sheen close about grazing.
